why: Tatoeba is attribution-only and its CC0 subset is 2,266 bytes for Spanish against 313,297 for French, so three of the four v1 languages cannot avoid the credits screen. A licence that requires attribution and has no reachable credit is a licence violation, not a missing UI nicety — and the half that matters on a device is `reachable`, because the builder is not what ships.
surface: S152, reachable from the report sheet S045 and About S137. S152 is NOT in deep/00-PRODUCT-MAP.md, which stops at S151; the map owes it a row before P4 renders it.
rule: `credits()` renders the `attribution:` rows of `meta` and nothing else. `creditsViolations()` walks `sentence` and `audio`, which `credits()` never reads, and reports anything attributed whose source or owner the surface does not carry. The two halves must stay computed from disjoint rows: a check derived from the query it is checking cannot fail.
note: Each case is a whole pack, not a diff: `credits` are the `attribution:` meta rows the build wrote, and `sentences`/`audio` are the tables it wrote beside them. `violations` is the EXACT sorted set of lines, never a count — one ownerless asset produces two facts (the asset, and the credits row that would render blank) and a test that counted them would pass on either alone.

cases.why: The clean case, and it is an assertion in its own right: a gate that only ever proves `no violations` passes just as well when the surface renders nothing at all. Five Tatoeba sentences under one credit, one Piper voice, one share-alike derived list.

EC-PACK-56 itself: a shipped sentence from an attribution-requiring corpus whose owner nobody recorded. Insertable only because the test drops the schema CHECK — a real pack refuses the row — and the scan must catch it anyway, because a constraint is not a substitute for the check that runs on what shipped.
violations: sentence s1 requires attribution and names no owner

cases.why: The reachability case, and the reason `credits()` may not scan `sentence`: the row names an owner, so the ownerless check is happy, but the build wrote no `attribution:` row for its corpus and S152 would render nothing about it. While `credits()` grouped this same table, no input could reach this line.
violations: sentence s1 cites tatoeba, which the credits surface does not render

cases.why: The corpus is credited, but to somebody else. A licence row edited in one place and not the other ships a credit that names the wrong party, which is a worse outcome than no credit at all.
violations: sentence s1 is attributed to Somebody else entirely, which the credits surface does not render

cases.why: Review R7: a voice engine's code licence is not its voices' licence. Piper is GPL-3.0 code whose one Japanese voice is CC BY-NC-SA, so the obligation rides per clip — and a whitespace owner is not an owner.
violations: voice clip a1 requires attribution and names no owner

cases.why: The voice reachability case. The clip names its owner and the surface renders a sentence credit, but nothing on S152 covers the engine — voices are credited once per engine (`voice:<engine>`), never once per clip, and the read side has to mint the same id the build does or it is comparing two vocabularies.
violations: voice clip a1 cites voice:piper, which the credits surface does not render

cases.why: A derived list that is share-alike and has no owner recorded. The frequency ordering reaches the learner as the order the units are taught in; it is neither a sentence nor a voice and has no row of its own anywhere else in the pack, which is exactly how it gets forgotten.
violations: derived list hermitdave requires attribution and names no owner

cases.why: CC0 text and an Apache-2.0 voice: nothing requires attribution, so an empty credits surface is correct rather than suspicious. Without this case the gate would be satisfiable by reporting every row.
